problems: claim 2 weakened: Teams that use asynchronous communication can gain a lot of productivity. (Degree is a claim: a plain word of the same force as 'significant' keeps it; dropping it or hardening 'can' fails.)  -  Requiring teams to commit to asynchronous communication narrows the claim from teams that use it.

claim 3 strengthened: Culture matters as well as tools. (The not-X-but-Y staging may go; the claim that culture counts stays.)  -  The rewrite adds dependency and says culture matters at least as much as tools.
added: 'those gains depend on culture at least as much as on tools'  -  The source does not say the gains depend on culture or compare culture's importance with tools.
added: 'nothing of yours in it yet, so it will still read as generic'  -  This adds an assessment of the rewrite and a claim about the reader's material.

added: 'What happened? Which tool, team or customer? What figures do you know? What do you think of it?'  -  These questions instruct the reader to supply events, examples, figures and opinions absent from the source.
